prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Freedom, Fairness, Trust – and a strong green thread – frame the Liberal Democrats’ real alternative to Labour’s centralism and the Conservatives’ unfairness. This fully costed programme rebalances power to citizens, prioritises opportunity and dignity from youth to old age, defends civil liberties, and hardwires environmental responsibility into every policy.

Fair, affordable funding
- Redirect around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish DTI subsidies; scrap ID cards; repurpose the Child Trust Fund to cut class sizes).
- A single net tax rise: 50% only on income above £100,000 to fund scrapping tuition and top‑up fees, free personal care, and lower local taxes.
- Replace Council Tax with a fair Local Income Tax, cutting the typical bill by ~£450.

NHS and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via more scans, extended hours, transparent waits; free eye/dental checks; fairer prescription exemptions.
- More frontline staff; axe arbitrary targets; empower locally accountable decision-making; improve NHS dentistry.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund money to cut infant and junior class sizes; extend wraparound care and Children’s Centres.
- Qualified teachers in core subjects; lighter, smarter assessment; stronger discipline support; world‑class vocational-academic 14–19 pathways; green every school.

Crime with liberty
- 10,000 extra police by cancelling ID cards; smarter tech to cut paperwork.
- Tough community payback for non‑violent offenders; tackle anti‑social behaviour; make prison work with education and skills.
- Repeal illiberal control-order regime; strengthen due process; admit intercept evidence; create a UK Border Force.
- A Single Equality Act and hate‑crime units; firm but fair asylum with the right to work.

Prosperity, not red tape
- Keep economic stability with independent scrutiny of the Budget; simplify taxes.
- Support small firms: sunset clauses on regulations, single inspectorate, small‑business rate relief; abolish the DTI and invest in skills and science.
- Raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000; managed migration to fill skills gaps.

Pensions and families
- A Citizen’s Pension: over £100 more per month from 75, linked to earnings; end mass means‑testing for a million pensioners.
- Eight in ten pensioners better off under Local Income Tax; stronger maternity pay; scrap the CSA and move enforcement to HMRC; fairer disability support.

Homes, services and rural fairness
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; curb second homes where they overwhelm markets; protect post offices; zero‑waste goal with 60% recycling in seven years.
- Fair farm-gate prices via a duty to trade fairly; CAP and fisheries reform; a Marine Act; stronger animal welfare; no commercial GM without safety.

Europe and the world
- Iraq was wrong; support a rapid transition to legitimate Iraqi self‑security and withdraw within the UN mandate timeline.
- Lead multilaterally through the UN and EU; support the EU Constitution via referendum; equip but not overstretch forces; pursue nuclear disarmament and curb the arms trade.
- Meet 0.7% aid by 2011; fair trade, debt relief, and sustainable development.

Transport and climate
- Fix rail with streamlined franchises and targeted upgrades; greener vehicle taxes and congestion charging; long‑term shift to road‑user charging; free off‑peak buses for pensioners/disabled; reform aviation taxes.
- At least 20% renewable electricity by 2020; no new nuclear; carbon‑based tax reform; an Environmental Responsibility Act; government procurement to go green.

Democracy you can trust
- Curb prime‑ministerial power with a War Powers Act and a Civil Service Act; cut ministers and departments; devolve power and funding fairly.
- Fair votes (STV) for Commons and councils; an elected second chamber; votes at 16; a BBC regulator accountable to Parliament.

10 good reasons: patients before targets; scrap student fees; 10,000 more police not ID cards; free personal care; cleaner transport and energy; smaller classes not child trust cheques; fair pensions not means‑tests; only one tax rise (on £100k+); fair local tax; never again on Iraq.
